validation.spatial_grouping: KMeans on per-site coordinate centroids -> GroupKFold; records of one site/profile always share a fold
validation.tuning: GridSearchCV inside every training fold (nested CV); imputation and scaling fitted on training folds only
validation.spatial_partition_note: The main comparison builds the spatial partition ONCE (KMeans seeded with --seed0) and reuses it for every model, seed and scheme, so random-vs-spatial is a paired comparison. The SD across seeds of a spatial-CV cell therefore measures learner randomness only and is exactly 0.000 for deterministic models (ridge, PLS). The two uncertainties the fixed partition hides are reported separately: where the block boundaries fall (results.partition_sensitivity, methods kmeans_seed and grid_offset) and how many blocks are used (results.block_sensitivity). Family kmeans_seed: 5 KMeans seeds at 10 blocks (partitions compared up to cluster renumbering, which is arbitrary) gave 4 distinct partition(s), so part of the spatial-score spread is fold-placement uncertainty. Family grid_offset: boundaries redrawn with a random rotation and grid origin at a 5x5 grain, 5 seed run(s) -> 5 distinct partition(s); spread: random forest R2 0.032 +/- 0.047; ridge R2 -21.371 +/- 16.979. Both families are in results.partition_sensitivity (per-partition rows in results.partition_rows, learner seed held constant), and the effect of the block COUNT is in results.block_sensitivity. Only the SPATIAL arm is run here, so none of these numbers is a validation gap: do not difference them against the random-CV column of the main table.

experiment_scope.note: Parallelism affects wall-clock only: every grid candidate is a separate seeded fit, so R2 is identical at n_jobs=1 and n_jobs=4 (checked). --quick additionally skips nested tuning; it is for tests, never for reported numbers.

partition_sensitivity.note: only the partition varied here: same learner seed and the fixed parameters chosen in E1, so no model-randomness or tuning variance is mixed in. A 0.000 SD with 4 distinct partition(s) means the spatial R2 did not move when the boundaries moved.

interval.method: split-conformal, blocks held out for calibration, scored on unseen spatial test blocks
interval.honest_note: The nominal 90% interval is calibrated on held-out spatial blocks and scored on test blocks never seen; coverage below 0.90 means the interval is too narrow for new areas.

limitations: No low-cost sensor data: features are laboratory wet-chemistry values that a sensor could in principle proxy. Nothing here has been measured with the planned hardware.
No Ugandan field validation: predictions have not been checked against any soil sampled for this project.
Not validated for agronomic decisions: rates, timing, or certification claims must not be made from this prototype.
Laboratory values carry lab-to-lab bias; replicate records are collapsed, so measurement error is under-represented relative to a real sensor.
Prediction intervals are marginal (one width for all inputs), not conditional on the feature values.
